title: Stablecoins in 2025: Developments and Financial Stability Implications
date_evidence: Washington: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, April 08, 2026, https://doi.org/10.17016/2380-7172.4020.
key_claim: Stablecoin aggregate market capitalisation reached $317 billion as of 6 April 2026, more than 50% growth since early 2025, though the market flattened out during the final quarter of 2025 and first quarter of 2026; the note identifies complex intermediation chains, vertical integration and accelerating retail adoption through digital-wallet partnerships as structural changes that deepen interconnections between stablecoins and the traditional financial system.
notes: Tier 1 Fed Board FEDS Note. Anchors the market-size and growth-flattening quantification and the stablecoin-TradFi integration point.

publisher: White House Council of Economic Advisers
title: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending
date_evidence: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending. The White House. April 8, 2026
key_claim: At baseline calibration the CEA model finds eliminating stablecoin yield increases bank lending by only $2.1 billion (0.02%) with a net welfare cost of $800 million; even stacking every worst-case assumption produces only $531 billion in additional aggregate lending, a 4.4% increase in bank loans as of 2025Q4, with community-bank lending rising at most $129 billion (6.7%); the GENIUS Act prohibits issuers from offering yield but does not explicitly prohibit affiliate or third-party arrangements.
notes: Tier 1 US government analysis. Primary sourced counter-argument: the official estimate that the disintermediation/credit effect is small. Also confirms the GENIUS Act yield-ban affiliate loophole.

title: Stablecoins: framing the debate (speech by Pablo Hernandez de Cos, BIS General Manager)
date_evidence: Speech at a Bank of Japan seminar Tokyo, 20 April 2026
key_claim: Stablecoins resemble narrow banks: a shift towards narrow banking through stablecoins would loosen the tight link between deposit-taking and lending that exists in a fractional reserve system, so a larger share of credit supply to the private sector would have to be provided by non-bank financial institutions; the global stablecoin market cap was around $315 billion in early April 2026 against roughly $8 trillion of US bank deposits; mitigating equilibrium effects exist but the distribution of deposits and credit would still shift.
verbatim_quote: A shift towards narrow banking through stablecoins would loosen the tight link between deposit-taking and lending that exists in a fractional reserve system.
notes: Tier 1 BIS. Core conceptual anchor for the narrow-banking framing and the NBFI credit-migration consequence.

publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
title: Stablecoin Disintermediation (Staff Reports, no. 1185)
date_evidence: Lee, Michael Junho, and Donny Tou. 2026. "Stablecoin Disintermediation." Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Reports, no. 1185, February.
key_claim: Using transaction-level data linking on-chain transactions to wholesale interbank payments, the paper documents the first evidence of liquidity-driven bank disintermediation: banks with stablecoin deposits experience large increases in payment demand and operate 'narrowly', requiring substantially larger reserve balances; even as beneficiaries of stablecoin growth, partner banks' loan share of assets contracts relative to peers.
verbatim_quote: Even as beneficiaries of stablecoin growth within the banking system, partner banks' loan share of assets contracts relative to peers.
notes: Tier 1 NY Fed Staff Report. Structural anchor (3-6m band): the load-bearing empirical finding that even banks capturing stablecoin flows lend a smaller share. Cited inline like any other source.

title: Next steps for GENIUS payment stablecoins
date_evidence: Next steps for GENIUS payment stablecoins. March 3, 2026
key_claim: Banks are concerned that stablecoins paying interest-like awards via affiliates will siphon away deposits and reduce their ability to extend credit; the Independent Community Bankers of America estimates community banks would lose $1.3 trillion in deposits and $850 billion in loans if stablecoins pay interest; the authors judge the resulting macroeconomic harm overstated because banks can securitize loans and other intermediaries can extend credit, and note a ban on affiliate/third-party interest will likely be circumvented; banks are responding with tokenized deposits.
notes: Tier 2 Brookings (Nellie Liang and William Dudley). Supplies the ICBA loss estimate, the tokenized-deposit bank response, and a second counter-argument voice that the credit-harm case is overstated.

title: A new strategy to contain stablecoin risks in the European Union
key_claim: MiCA requires stablecoin issuers to hold 30%, or 60% for 'significant' issuers, of reserves as bank deposits and bans interest-bearing stablecoins more broadly than GENIUS, which creates a remuneration loophole; Bruegel argues the disintermediation fear is overblown because stablecoin issuance does not change total banking-system deposits and the central bank can recycle reserves to credit-creating institutions, so aggregate credit capacity need not change; euro-area bank excess liquidity was around EUR 2.3 trillion at end-Q1 2026.
notes: Tier 2 Bruegel (Reichlin, Sangers, Zettelmeyer). Strongest version of the equilibrium counter-argument and the US-EU regulatory-contrast source for geographic scope.

title: U.S. Treasury may boost T-Bill issuance as stablecoins eye $2 trillion market cap: StanChart
key_claim: Standard Chartered expects the stablecoin market cap to reach $2 trillion by end-2028, generating around $1 trillion in fresh Treasury bill demand; combined with projected Fed buying, new T-bill demand could reach $2.2 trillion against $1.3 trillion of supply, a $0.9 trillion gap; the total stablecoin market was roughly $300-320 billion in early 2026, up from $238 billion in April 2025, with post-GENIUS issuance having stalled; the Treasury's 4 February 2026 Quarterly Refunding Announcement said it is monitoring growing private-sector demand for Treasury bills.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism reporting a Standard Chartered research note. Anchors the stablecoin-as-marginal-T-bill-buyer thread and the growth-stalled counter-evidence.
